subject: environmental-science
intro: Environmental science leads to the careers that measure, protect and plan for the natural world — pollution control, conservation, environmental engineering and land-use planning.

roles.title: Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
roles.what: Identify, investigate and help eliminate sources of pollution and hazards that affect the environment or public health, working from measurements of air, food, soil, water and other sources.
roles.where: Water pollution (unit 3), air quality and climate (unit 4) and the sustainability-metrics-and-lca lessons teach the measure-then-recommend cycle the job is built on; fieldwork (5.4) adds the practice.

roles.title: Environmental Engineers
roles.what: Research, design and run engineering solutions to environmental hazards — waste treatment, site remediation and pollution-control technology for air, water and land.
roles.where: Unit 3's water supply and pollution topics — oil and plastic pollution included — plus waste-and-the-circular-economy and mitigation-and-adaptation-design lessons are the design briefs.

roles.title: Conservation Scientists
roles.what: Manage, improve and protect natural resources — conducting soil surveys, planning against soil erosion and advising farmers and ranchers on practices that conserve soil and water.
roles.where: Land unit 2 — soils and crop growth, food production, soil erosion — with ecosystems, biodiversity and fieldwork (unit 5) gives the soil-science and field-assessment grounding the role needs.

roles.title: Environmental Science and Protection Technicians, Including Health
roles.what: Perform laboratory and field tests to monitor the environment and investigate sources of pollution, collecting samples of gases, soil, water and other materials for testing.
roles.where: The fieldwork investigations of topic 5.4 and the water-pollution and air-quality lessons train the sampling-and-testing routine; natural hazards (unit 6) adds the risk awareness field work demands.

roles.title: Urban and Regional Planners
roles.what: Develop comprehensive plans for how towns, cities, counties and metropolitan areas use land and physical facilities, balancing development, environment and community needs.
roles.where: Human population (unit 7) — density, distribution and management — with land-soils-and-food-production and natural-hazards lessons supply the environmental constraints planners weigh when zoning.
